figures.title: The sliding window keeps only the last W keys in each row
figures.caption: With W = 4, each query scores only the four most recent keys including itself; earlier keys are masked out of the softmax and never read. The band slides down one row per token, so the work per token is W rather than n. At n = 130,659 and W = 4,096 the windowed path computes 535,179,264 pairs against 8,535,952,470 for full causal attention, 16x fewer.
figures.alt: A ten-by-ten mask grid. Row i has a 1 in columns i minus 3 through i and blank cells elsewhere, so the ones form a diagonal band that slides right as rows go down. The last row is highlighted and shows ones in columns 6 through 9. Blank cells are masked and never enter the softmax denominator.

data.note: Schematic 10 x 10 grid with W = 4. In the deployment W = 4,096; the band has 4,096 cells per row and the mask is applied tile by tile.

figures.title: Three patterns and what each costs
figures.caption: Full causal attention computes 8,535,952,470 pairs at n = 130,659. A sliding window of 4,096 computes 535,179,264 pairs, 16x fewer, and after 32 layers reaches 131,041 positions. Dilation 2 covers 8,191 positions with the same 4,096 scores per query; a hybrid of 16 full and 16 local layers costs 51.6 percent of an all-full stack.
figures.alt: Three aligned panels. Full causal lists 8,535,952,470 pairs at n = 130,659, every query reading every earlier key, with cost growing as n squared. The sliding window with W = 4,096 lists 535,179,264 pairs, 16 times fewer, a receptive field of 131,041 after 32 layers, and a cache holding only the last W positions. Dilated and global lists dilation 2 covering 8,191 positions with 4,096 scores, global tokens attended by every token, and a 16-full-plus-16-local hybrid at 51.6 percent of full cost.

panels.title: Full causal vs sliding window
panels.note: Full cost grows with n squared; the window costs W per token. The path back to position 1 is indirect, carried through 32 layers of averaging.

panels.note: A full layer gives every token a direct edge; a local layer does not. That difference is what retrieval tests measure.

figures.title: A rolling cache holds W positions, not the whole context
figures.caption: Mistral 7B's cache costs 128 KiB per token: 32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 dimensions x 2 for K and V x 2 bytes. A 4,096-token window needs 512 MiB per stream, where holding 65,536 positions would need 8 GiB and the mean 130,659-token prompt 16 GiB. The last two bars are 128 KiB multiplied by the position count, not separately measured sizes.
figures.alt: Three horizontal bars of cache size per stream. The rolling window of 4,096 positions is 512 MiB. A full cache over one stream's 65,536-position share is 8 GiB. A full cache over the mean 130,659-token prompt is 16 GiB.

data.note: 128 KiB per token = 32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 x 2 (K/V) x 2 bytes. The rolling buffer writes token i to slot i mod W; position ids stay absolute so the mask still knows the true distance.
